issues.title: node:sqlite marked stable
issues.html:
#​649 — November 26, 2026


Read on the Web







Your Tools Are Hiding npm Audits From You — Running npm audit over a fresh Next.js app can show zero vulnerabilities, but a separate audit of its bundled dependencies tells a different story. Zach shows how Next.js can 'sweep audits under the rug' by vendoring dependencies, and has built 📊 Prototype Pollution Report to rank popular frameworks' packages based on their audit results.

Zach Leatherman



Instant Postgres Branches for Every Agent Run — ClickHouse acquired Xata to bring instant branching, cloning, and scale-to-zero to ClickHouse Managed Postgres, now GA on local NVMe and up to 10x faster. Start with $300 in free credits.

ClickHouse Managed Postgres sponsor



node:sqlite is Now Marked Stable — More than two years after its experimental debut, Node's built-in SQLite module is now marked stable as of today's latest Node 27 alpha (0.2.0). No native addon is required.

Node.js



IN BRIEF:

  • AWS Lambda now supports Node.js 26 as a managed runtime (for both Web and Event functions) and container base image (for Event Functions only).

  • ⚠️ Several Fastify plugins have had a flurry of security fixes, including critical middleware bypasses in @fastify/express and @fastify/middie, and request smuggling in @fastify/reply-from.

  • 💡 An open PR proposes adding a built-in pprof CPU profiler to Node, ported from Datadog's work, with reviewers debating the approach.

  • Node's main branch now uses Ada 4.1, a notably faster release of the URL parser behind URL.

  • 🤖 Vercel's eve, a Next.js-style agent framework we featured in June, has reached 1.0. The idea is for you to 'own the harness' you build agents on.

  • 🇺🇸 CascadiaJS 2027 is taking place in Seattle next June and its CFP is open till January 10 (curiously you can even submit your talk via an MCP server!).



How I Fixed 55 Bugs in a Week by Making My Monorepo More Agent-Friendly — Inkdrop is a fantastic Electron-based note taking app I've been using for years, so it's cool to see how its creator has reshaped it for his agents to work on. Feature folders, strict lint rules, and new tests added extra discipline, surfacing a variety of long-standing bugs.

Takuya Matsuyama



Do Agents Really Do Better With TypeScript? — It's often claimed types can make coding agents produce better code, but Evil Martians found across three public benchmarks that agents solved comparable JavaScript issues at least as often as TypeScript issues.

Irina Nazarova (Evil Martians)



📄 Ranking Languages and Runtimes by MIME Base64 Decoding Speed – Node, Bun and Deno all sit near the top, largely thanks to Daniel's simdutf. Daniel Lemire

📄 Finding a Memory Leak in a Production NestJS App Kamil Mysliwiec

📄 5 Steps to Refactor a Fastify App for Testing and Growth Liran Tal



🛠 Code & Tools





Jimp 2: Image Processing in Plain JavaScript — One of the more delightful homepages we've seen! Jimp is a library for working with images in Node or the browser with no native dependencies. After a quiet couple of years, 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 landed this week, fixing long-standing quirks and adding a drawing API. There's a playground if you want to kick the tires.

Jimp



💡 If you want a smaller option, ImageScript 4.0 can, unlike Jimp, read/write WebP, AVIF and JPEG XL in pure TypeScript, no WASM needed.



Anyone Can Claim to Be Claude Duet. Here's How to Spot the Real One — A User-Agent header is just text. Fingerprint identifies Claude Duet so you can set rules for login and checkout. Learn how.

Fingerprint sponsor



Reintroducing Stricli: Bloomberg's Framework for Type-Safe CLIs — Bloomberg builds its internal command line tools with Stricli. As well as first-class type support (which feeds into auto-generated help and error messages), your commands' code can also be lazy-loaded for added efficiency.

Michael Molisani and Jeff Posnick (Bloomberg)



binary-parser 3.0: Declaratively Build Parsers for Binary Data — Chain methods like .uint16be() and .bit4() to describe a binary format, and you end up with a parser as fast as a bespoke one. There are some examples for parsing ELF, TCP, tar, and similar formats.

Keichi Takahashi



  • Flatbush 4.9 – A fast static spatial index approach for 2D points and rectangles. Indexing is now up to 2.7x faster on large inputs.

  • memoize-one 7.0 – A memoization library that only caches the result of the most recent arguments.

  • DOMPurify 3.5 – Fast XSS sanitizer for HTML, MathML and SVG, usable server-side with jsdom.

  • ioredis 6.1 – Popular performance-focused Redis client.

  • Awilix 14.0 – Dependency injection container for Node.

issues.title: Time-travel debugging for Node
issues.html:
#​648 — November 19, 2026


Read on the Web







🤖 node-skills: Teach Your Coding Agent About Modern Node.js — LLMs can fail to use features that Node has recently added unless you provide a little extra guidance. James's agent skills augment your harness with the likes of node:sqlite, node:ffi, the permission model and new test runner features.

James M Snell



Build AI Agents That Don’t Burn Your Token Budget — Most AI problems don't need a swarm of agents. Bri Goldfarb from the GitHub Copilot team shows you how to weigh context, reliability, and cost, then build the simplest architecture that works in JavaScript.

Master.dev sponsor



vlt Opens Its npm Mirror to Everyone — Clean installs can spend a lot of time downloading npm package metadata. vlt's mirror of the npm registry, however, serves much less metadata resulting in installs running anywhere from 20-70% faster. An account/token is no longer needed, so you can try it from npm, pnpm, Yarn, etc. with a quick config change.

Erick Wendel (vlt)



💡 If you're switching registries, pnpm 12.22 now rechecks your release-age and trust policies against whichever registry you switch to.



IN BRIEF:

  • Node already bundles simdjson, and its co-creator, Daniel Lemire, has proposed a node:json module to expose it for faster, lazier JSON parsing.

  • 💰 The OpenJS Foundation is launching the OpenJS Ad Network as a way to raise funds for its various projects, including Node, Express and Fastify. The good news is it will use no behavioral targeting or third-party tracking.

  • If you're running a long-lived HTTP server on Node 24, there's a setting you'll want to check. A team traced steady memory growth to 24.18's larger default Buffer.poolSize, which setting it back to 8192 resolved.

  • Node allows TLS 1.2 renegotiation by default, but it's being deprecated. The plan is to disable it by default in Node 27, with opt-in support (via the allowRenegotiation option) for legacy servers.



Express is Now Observable by Design — Bye-bye monkey patching! Express 5's router now publishes a Node TracingChannel for all middleware, route handlers and router.param() callbacks so APMs (or your own code) can subscribe from anywhere to get timings, errors and route patterns.

Abdelrahman Awad (Express)



💡 On a related note, OpenTelemetry's JavaScript SDK 3.0 is out. It now requires Node 22.15+, ships proper ESM and CommonJS exports, and makes logs stable.



How Green Threads Would Work in Node — Last week we covered James's PR adding an experimental node:green_threads module to Node. Here, he blogs about how they work, how they compare to worker threads and vm contexts, and the limitations of the approach.

James M Snell



Why Resend Moved Its Email API from Node to Go — An interesting case study from a popular email service provider well known for its JavaScript roots. Sharp reductions in memory and CPU use were the clearest wins.

Resend



Stop Reinstalling node_modules on Every CI Run — WarpBuild snapshot runners start with your toolchain already in place. Try it with $50 in free credits using START50.

WarpBuild sponsor



📄 Profiling a Node Site Build: Event Loop Utilization per Phase – The 57% of 'idle' time was a missing cache. Maris Stella Labs

📄 Every Security Weakness Matters When Vulnerability Chaining Is King Liran Tal

📊 Load Testing an Express App on Node 26, Bun 1.4 and Deno 2.9 Huseyin Babal



🛠 Code & Tools





Replay Node 26: Time-Travel Debugging for Node — Wouldn't it be neat if you could add a console.log after a bug crops up? Replay's "time-travel" Node build can make it possible, and Mark shows it recording a Next.js server, then pulling out values the app didn't originally log. Note that it's Linux x86-64 only and uploading your own recordings requires a (free) account.

Mark Erikson (Replay)



🔒 Secretlint 14: A Linter to Catch Credentials Before You Commit — A linter that looks for API keys, tokens and other secrets in your code. A very useful tool if you're letting agents commit your code! The homepage shows how you can get started with a single npx.

Secretlint Team



npkill 1.0: Not Just for node_modules Any More — npx npkill has long been a great way to clean up big node_modules folders, but it now supports other ecosystems and build artefacts, like those created by Next.js and Python.

Juan Torres



BrowserPod 4.0: Run Node and pnpm Inside a Browser Tab — A WebAssembly microVM that runs unmodified Node.js 22, npm and pnpm 12 in the browser. It's now free to use, and you can try it on a Vite project right away.

Leaning Technologies



  • Node.js 27.0 Alpha 0.1 – Adds X.509 certificate and CSR generation to node:crypto, as well as subprocess.timedOut. Alpha 0.1.1 followed, adding a notarized binary for macOS users.

  • 🎬 Mediabunny 1.66 – A powerful toolkit for reading/writing/converting media files in Node and the browser. Gets many fixes and improvements found during a long AI-assisted audit.

  • 🔒 ws 8.23 – The popular WebSocket client and server library fixes a memory exhaustion vulnerability triggered by flooding a connection with pings.

  • semantic-release 26 – Automated versioning and package publishing tool (homepage). Now requires Node 26.13+ and bundles npm 12.

  • nano-spawn 3.0, quick-lru 8.0, debounce 4.0 and crypto-hash 5.0 – New majors of four of Sindre Sorhus's small utilities, all now requiring Node 22.

  • nvm 0.41 – The Node version manager now understands Node's new alpha release channel.

  • onvif 1.1 – ONVIF (a common standard used by IP cameras) client library.



📰 Classifieds



🎬 Your app needs video, not a video team. Upload any format to Hyperserve's API, get back MP4 on a global CDN. Ship video in an afternoon.

Odds-API.io: Real-time sports odds from 450+ bookmakers over REST and WebSocket, with an official Node.js SDK and an MCP server for AI agents.

CodeAF adds 27 MB of RAM per coding session, 8x less than Claude Code, so 16 fit in half a gigabyte. #1 on DeepSWE, lowest cost per fix.



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem



  • 📊 e18e is tracking server-side rendering performance across frameworks including Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, SvelteKit, and TanStack Start.

  • 🔒 Bun 1.4.5 is a security release with many fixes impacting its implementations of Node APIs like node:tls, node:http, node:https, node:dns, node:quic and node:zlib.

  • Text.js renders React apps inside the browser's DevTools console. It supports keyboard input, routing, and Suspense. One demo recreates OpenCode's terminal UI inside console.log. Why? I'm still not sure.

  • jQuery 4.1 and 3.8 are out. 4.1 exposes redirect URLs, serializes form-associated custom elements, and speeds up uniqueSort. 3.8 backports numerous fixes and deprecates APIs removed in 4.0.

issues.title: 22 Node, Bun and Deno stacks benchmarked
issues.html:
#​647 — November 12, 2026


Read on the Web







An Experimental 'Green Threads' Implementation for Node — James has opened a PR that adds a new, lightweight kind of worker that shares a small pool of OS threads, with each worker getting its own V8 isolate (but no Node APIs). His numbers show a thousand of them using about 1GB of memory vs 6.7GB for regular worker threads. Early days, but a promising idea that deserves feedback.

James M Snell



Debug Errors and Agents Faster: Sentry Changelog Live — A walkthrough of what’s new for debugging errors and performance issues, including fixing production bugs with Seer and tracing the agents you build. Live Q&A. Nov 18, 10am PT. Save your spot.

Sentry sponsor



🔒 This Week's Node.js Security Releases — Node v26.13.1, v24.22.3 and v22.23.5 patch a lot of HTTP/2 and TLS flaws, plus others in zlib and the permission model (seven are rated 'high' in severity). The worst bug can allow a remote client to read memory belonging to other connections. v26 and v24 also get last week's Undici fixes.

The Node.js Project



🤖 Five of the bugs were reported by Chris Rohlf "in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research", with another credited to Trail of Bits (OpenAI).



What's New in Node.js 27 — The co-author of Node.js Design Patterns has put together an example-led tour of the latest (alpha) Node release, going from the new iterator helpers and promise-based node:net/promises API to the now-unflagged virtual file system, plus the v27 breaking changes to get prepared for.

Luciano Mammino



IN BRIEF:

  • The browser-style Web Worker API is now enabled by default on Node's main branch, so expect it in a future Node 27 alpha release.

  • Sadly, JavaScript function hosting platform Val Town is winding down. Tom MacWright, who advocated for its move to Deno (from vm2), wrote this week about that choice saying Deno's sandbox never let them down.

  • Netlify has introduced Netlify Server, a long-running Node-powered backend process for WebSockets and in-memory state, now in early access.

  • An open PR proposes a built-in node:yaml module for parsing YAML.

  • 📊 The State of JavaScript 2026 survey is now open to take.



How X is Rebuilding Its Web App on Fastify and Node 26 — X is replacing three servers with one built on Fastify and Platformatic Watt, running worker threads on Node 26. Yagiz covers the streaming architecture, the event loop stalls they had to fix, and how it's making X faster on the Web.

Yagiz Nizipli (X Engineering)



Keep Your CI Workflow While Upgrading the Runner at Half the Cost — Switch to a WarpBuild runner in your Node job and see faster builds. Try it with $50 in free credits using START50.

WarpBuild sponsor



A Malicious npm Release, Published via Trusted Publishing — A tour of the process and code behind the recent hijacking of Ethersphere's bee-js release process and how a backdoored version was published with valid provenance.

Socket Research Team



Your JS Error Is Lying to You — If you've ever seen "err":{} logged for an error that definitely had a message, Gábor's look into what an Error loses between creation and the log line could be helpful.

Gábor Koós



🛠 Code & Tools





forges: One Client for GitHub, GitLab and Other Git Forges — From Nuxt's lead maintainer, this is a single typed client for working with issues, PRs, notifications, checks and webhooks across GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Codeberg, Gitea, Azure DevOps and more.

Daniel Roe



AWS Emulator: An Official Local Emulator for AWS APIs — It's built in Rust, but there's now an officially supported way to point your AWS SDK or CLI at a local endpoint covering hundreds of its service interfaces. In the release post, Amazon suggests it's largely aimed at agents, while also revealing the emulator itself was built with agents (and how).

Amazon Web Services



chrome-capture: Record a Chrome Tab at 60 FPS to MP4 — A neat, compact tool you can run with npx to record a Chrome 153+ tab at high quality to an MP4 file with no ffmpeg needed.

Paul Irish



  • Playwright 1.65 – Microsoft's browser automation library. Its test runner can now run under Bun too (with a few caveats), and there are a few potentially breaking changes for existing users who upgrade…

  • vlt 1.7 – The package manager adds vlt deploy for copying a workspace and production dependencies into a standalone folder, and now pins git dependencies to a commit.

  • Postgres.js 4.1 – Follows the recent big 4.0 release with sql.batch(), a query_timeout option, and restored Node 18 support.



📰 Classifieds



⏱️ JSON in Postgres: still fast at 1M rows? ExoBench benchmarks your query at scale, from Claude or Cursor. Now in preview.

🔓 Your auth validates once at login. After that, a stolen cookie works from anywhere. Fingerprint catches it. Try it free.



📊  22 JavaScript Stack Combos Benchmarked





▶ I Tested Every JavaScript Runtime — A fun benchmark of the same Postgres-backed API app running on Node, Bun and Deno using each of their popular frameworks. In his tests, runtime choice made a bigger difference than framework choice. The code and full results are on GitHub too.

Arjay McCandless
